candidates: Test functions that verify a specific physical or behavioral property should include a docstring that names that property explicitly (e.g., 'center of mass does not drift during dynamics'), not just describe the mechanism or subject being exercised; the function name alone rarely conveys enough intent.

When a variable must be stored as an instance attribute rather than a local variable because an external system (e.g., Asap's atom-migration mechanism) accesses it by name between two points in a method, add an inline comment at the declaration site explaining this constraint — otherwise the variable looks like a refactoring target and the requirement will be silently broken.

When code has an implicit interface contract with an external library (e.g., Asap requires specific instance attributes to be present after each MD step so it can register them with its migration mechanism), add a dedicated unit test that explicitly enumerates and asserts each required attribute, so a violation produces a clear, descriptive failure rather than surfacing only in a hard-to-reproduce parallel integration run.
